findings.text: The ordering assertion `refs.index("alpha#s1") < refs.index("beta#s1")` cannot fail on the term it is meant to test: the section key falls through to identity (roadmap_ranking.py:302 index 7), and "alpha#s1" < "beta#s1" preserves the order, so dropping the ROI term from _priority_key leaves the assertion green. Only line 300 is a guard for the ROI claim.

The same shape: `_refs(result).index("twin#s1") < _refs(result).index("twin#s2")` is also satisfied by the identity tie-break ("twin#s1" < "twin#s2"), so it does not discriminate the stuck signal's effect on rank. The stuck claim is carried by the two `stuck` assertions and line 350, not by line 351.

The docstring calls the returned tuple the least favourable key the row admits, but index 6 is set to 0.0 while lower is better for effort (roadmap_ranking.py:302, _priority_key orders remaining_effort_hours ascending), so the floor's effort is the most favourable, not the least. The effect is intended — the last section row can never report `effort` — but the prose says the opposite of the arithmetic and a future reader adjusting this floor would be misled.
